purpose: Pause the opening-hand countdown under covering panels and respect current motion preferences when canceling or restoring startup presentation.
head: 0f08fb47bb8637ccf082f406d69f6f6c0cbe7b52
changes: OpeningDeal listens to its owner's relevant property changes: stop the countdown while covered and restart the reading interval after the last covering panel closes.
Turning motion off cancels both armed and visible opening presentation, without clearing the pending identity or submitting commands.
Tutorial return restores armed/visible startup presentation only when current motion remains enabled.
Dispose removes the local property subscription before stopping and detaching the opening timer.
Add regression branches to the existing table shortcut and modal focus checks; document the resulting behavior.

coveredTimerCoverage.host: Existing real VM and MainWindow command/shortcut fixture, using the owning actual DispatcherTimer on the WPF dispatcher.
assertions: Each covering panel remains open; opening IDs and current engine reference/all eight viewer-safe snapshots remain unchanged after a dispatcher pump.
The actual opening timer is disabled with no Tick while covered; Escape resumes it after the panel closes.
Settings above a retained gallery keeps the timer paused after closing only settings; closing the gallery resumes it.
Once uncovered, the real timer ticks exactly once, hides opening presentation and clears faces, while all eight player views remain unchanged.
coveredTimerCoverage.cleanup: Tick observer is removed and the original Interval restored in finally; monitor timers stop in finally; enclosing Window closes and the VM disposes.
limitations: The 50 ms accelerated real-timer check verifies pause/resume/one natural expiry; it does not measure the default 1800 ms desktop reading duration.
Identity, general-selection and result coverage is included in the implementation's predicate, without added real-timer regression branches for these three layers.
The shortcut fixture drives actual VM commands and the shared key handler; it is not a foreground desktop input acceptance test.

motionCoverage.host: Real loaded MainWindow, offscreen and native-hidden with no foreground ownership; actual bound SettingsMotionToggle.OnClick activates the preference.
assertions: Disabling motion during an armed start preserves identity/engine/all eight viewer-safe snapshots, then confirming identity/general does not display the pending opening.
Disabling motion while opening is visible clears its faces and preserves the engine and every player's view.
Re-enabling motion after cancellation does not replay a retired opening.
Disabling motion during practice prevents restoration of both visible and armed original startup animation, while preserving original engine and safe player views.
Pending original identity still restores after tutorial return with motion disabled.

review.notes: Initialization does not access an unready snapshot; pending/general and game-over state use value-change notifications; same-value view refreshes do not reset the countdown. Covering-state checks, current motion guards and local observer/timer cleanup remain on the existing UI/session boundaries.
